headline: New Zealand’s Party Vote and Seat Count Still Point Different Ways
deck: Labour leads the preliminary party vote, while National holds more seats; special votes leave New Zealand’s next government unsettled.
body: Labour led National in New Zealand’s preliminary party vote, 29.3% to 29.2%, while National held 42 seats to Labour’s 36 under the mixed-member proportional system. [E1]
The Guardian reported that 66 seats appeared necessary for a majority and that it was unclear whether either the left or right bloc could assemble one. [E2]
On the current tally, the right bloc could form a government, but the count is incomplete. [E3]
Special votes in New Zealand typically skew left. [E4]
CNN described Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National-led coalition as having a paper-thin majority in Saturday’s preliminary results. [E5]
Luxon told supporters in Auckland that National appeared to have a pathway to form the next government, while calling the race “too close to call.” [E6]
The preliminary numbers put the right-wing coalition grouping on 67 seats in a 131-seat parliament, with nearly 400,000 special votes still uncounted. [E7]
CNN projected the opposition grouping of Labour, the Greens and Te Pati Māori at 57 seats. [E8]
